title: Frémont and Kit Carson across the Great Basin and the Sierra, 1843–44
summary: Frémont's second expedition left the Missouri frontier in May 1843 and went by the Oregon Trail to Fort Vancouver on the Columbia, then south by Pyramid Lake. It crossed the Sierra Nevada in midwinter, in January and February 1844, with Kit Carson, and reached Sutter's Fort. It went home by the Old Spanish Trail, Utah Lake and Bent's Fort.

events.text: Men and animals were near starvation in deep snow. With Carson guiding, the expedition came down to Sutter's Fort in March. Frémont's report, with Charles Preuss's map, appeared in 1845; Congress had ten thousand copies printed.
